conventions.testing: Unit tests in #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks within each language file; tests use tree_sitter::Query and QueryCursor for query validation
conventions.linting: clippy with -D warnings; clippy.toml configured; deny.toml for cargo-deny checks
conventions.error_handling: thiserror for custom errors; Option and Result types; unwrap_used/expect_used denied in clippy

patterns: LanguageInfo struct with name, language, element_query, call_query, reference_query, import_query, impl_query, impl_trait_query, defuse_query, and handler fields
get_language_info() match on lang_name returning LanguageInfo with module::QUERY constants
get_ts_language() match on lang_name returning tree_sitter_X::LANGUAGE.into()
EXTENSION_MAP as const slice of (extension, lang) tuples in lang.rs
DEFUSE_QUERY pattern: local_variable_declaration, assignment_expression, update_expression, identifier captures
constraints: tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 depends on tree-sitter-language ^0.1.0 only; tree-sitter is dev-only
defuse_query is mandatory (Option<&'static str>) - every language sets it
No feature flags for languages; unconditional compilation
Swift uses class_declaration with declaration_kind field (class/struct/actor/enum/extension), not separate node types
test_coverage: Existing language files (java.rs, kotlin.rs, go.rs) have comprehensive unit tests: query validity, extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance, defuse_query write sites. Swift should follow same pattern.

approaches.name: Direct Java Model
approaches.description: Create swift.rs mirroring java.rs structure: ELEMENT_QUERY (function_declaration, class_declaration, protocol_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (local_variable_declaration, assignment_expression, identifier), extract_inheritance walking inheritance_specifier->inherits_from->user_type/type_identifier
cons: Swift has no separate struct/enum nodes - handled via declaration_kind field
No impl blocks - set to None

approaches.name: Kotlin-Inspired Hybrid
approaches.description: Use kotlin.rs as secondary reference for protocol handling; Kotlin has separate interface_declaration like Swift has protocol_declaration

recommendation: Direct Java Model - Swift shares JVM-inspired structural patterns (named declarations, type inheritance, imports). The class_declaration with declaration_kind field handles struct/enum/actor/extension uniformly, simplifying ELEMENT_QUERY. DEFUSE_QUERY follows java.rs pattern exactly.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-swift node-types.json: class_declaration contains inheritance_specifier children. Each inheritance_specifier has an 'inherits_from' field pointing to user_type or function_type. Extract type_identifier text from user_type node. Multiple specifiers are siblings under class_declaration.
